prompt: A cyber attack took down our payment-processing for six hours. Walk us through DORA classification and reporting.
assertions: Classifies against the major-incident criteria of CDR (EU) 2024/1772 (clients/counterparties affected, duration/downtime, geographic spread, data losses, criticality of services, economic impact)

Gives the three-stage reporting timeline per Art. 19 and CDR (EU) 2025/301: initial notification within 4 hours of classification (and no later than 24 hours from awareness), intermediate report within 72 hours, final report within one month
Identifies the recipient: the competent financial supervisory authority (lex specialis — not the NIS2 CSIRT channel for financial entities)
Mentions client/user communication duties where the incident affects clients' financial interests
Adds useful context accurately if used: ESAs' first annual report (June 2026) counted 3,383 major ICT incidents for 2025, ~two-thirds with no or minor client disruption
